title: Paragraph Headings Relocated (Option 3: run-in heading kept inline; only the label relocated)

illustrates.quote: Changing Paragraph Headings to Cell-5 or Cell-7 Headings. A paragraph heading may provide better navigation for the braille reader when it is separated from the paragraph and changed to a cell-5 or cell-7 heading. (See Sample 4-5: Paragraph Headings Relocated on page 4-20 and Sample 4-6: Paragraph Heading Changed to Cell-5 Heading on page 4-21.)

blocks.features: Small bold banner label with a rolled-scroll icon, above the run-in heading; relocated onto its own cell-5 line in every option including this one.

braille.notes: Line 1 the cell-5 heading 'Connection to History'; line 2 the paragraph opens immediately (no blank line) with 'The tree of life' wrapped in a typeform/emphasis indicator pair ("@#7...@#'"), left inline, then continues as running text.

uncertain: Emboss's real translator renders this run-in heading's typeform bracket as "^7...^'" for **bold** markup (byte-identical to Example 4-6's confirmed bold lead-in phrase elsewhere in this section), but the source's own braille here reads "@#7...@#'" -- a different bracket pair neither plain bold, plain italic (".7....'" ), nor underline ("_7..._'") reproduces. Not resolved further here (see standards-findings.md); flagged for Paul. Every other line of this file matches exactly once the systematic heading->paragraph flush-indent finding is set aside.

The Darwin paragraph directly follows the relocated heading(s) with no blank line; Emboss's formatPara still applies its ordinary 2-cell first-line indent rather than starting flush at column 1 as the gold braille does -- see standards-findings.md F-39. Expect a documented mismatch limited to this indent, not a content bug.
